packageRules.description: Patch and minor bumps of the data layer are safe to batch; CI installs the chart in a real kind cluster before any of them can merge.
Majors get their own PR. Postgres 18 moved its data directory - a major bump here is a behaviour change, never a version string change.
The kind node image decides the Kubernetes version. Always alone, always read the kind release notes first.
Go toolchain: go.mod, the Dockerfile builder and CI's GO_VERSION must move together or CI fails on the first run.
Actions are low risk and noisy; batch them.

customManagers.description: kindest/node, which no standard manager understands. Both cluster files AND ci.yml: the e2e job pins node_image separately, and if it lags behind, CI validates a Kubernetes version nobody runs.
Argo CD, pinned in the Makefile and installed from a versioned manifest URL.
protoc plugin versions, pinned identically in the Makefile, the Dockerfile and CI.

CI's Go version. No standard manager sees it, and it has to move together with go.mod and the Dockerfile builder - otherwise the toolchain PR arrives with setup-go on the old version and the first step fails with 'go.mod requires go >= ...'. Trimmed to major.minor to match how it is written.
The helm binary CI installs. This is a `with:` input, so the github-actions manager - which only reads `uses:` refs - never touches it.
The kind binary CI installs, same blind spot as helm. Note this is kind itself, not kindest/node - the two version independently.
